target_customer: Low income and prepaid mobile users in Indian cities who buy Wi-Fi data in small units, plus local cable operators and shop owners who host the hotspots
problem: Affordable, fast internet access was out of reach for many Indian users, and mobile data costs and poor connectivity drove app churn.
business_model: Prepaid sachet data sales over a distributed Wi-Fi network, with revenue shared with local cable operator partners and later token incentives
product_category: Decentralised broadband and Wi-Fi infrastructure (later DePin)

founders.name: Karam Lakshman
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder with the headline Tech at wifidabba.com and says the founders worked in the mobile app industry for a decade. A search summary of the company About page (not opened by me) says he led an internet and mobile fund at the IIM Ahmedabad incubation centre and founded Mildly Classic; treated as unverified.

founders.name: Shubhendu Sharma
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder building dabba.com. A search summary of the About page (not opened) mentions Mahindra British Telecom and the IIMA incubation centre; unverified.

technical_complexity.rationale: Free space optics laser links, custom hardware nodes and a prepaid access system were hard for a small team, per the YC description and Wikipedia coverage of its proprietary Supernode devices.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and local cable operator relationships take time to copy, but connectivity resale was open to telcos and other hotspot operators.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cheap mobile data from Jio from late 2016 pressured paid Wi-Fi demand. Sources found do not show incumbents copying the model.

market_need_then: Indian regulators were consulting on public Wi-Fi in 2016 and early 2017 (TRAI open house on 9 January 2017), and only about 31,500 public hotspots existed, which signalled unmet access demand.

branding.domain_note: The YC listing shows the company now uses dabba.com, having used wifidabba.com earlier. No purchase detail found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain mass market language about cheap sachet internet, per YC description and YourStory headline

branding.brand_signature: Sachetization of internet access, a one gigabyte at a time price idea

rebrands.why: Reported by thin sources as an evolution to Dabba Network and the dabba.com domain with a crypto and Web3 focus; date and reason not sourced

branding.community_and_virality: YourStory covered the consumer launch with a headline comparing its price to cutting chai; no evidence of merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press coverage only and no sourced evidence of a brand driving growth.

pivots.from: Free space optics Wi-Fi sold as prepaid sachets
pivots.to: Crypto and blockchain based decentralised connectivity (Dabba Network)
pivots.why: YC description states the vision to be the connectivity layer for Web3; date not sourced

outcome_analysis: Wifi Dabba is still listed as active and joined India's PM WANI public Wi-Fi program, installing about 430 access points in Bangalore according to Wikipedia. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff reporting was found. Public funding information is thin and conflicting, so its financing path and whether the sachet model scaled against cheap Jio mobile data cannot be judged from sources found.
notes: Company website redirected to en.dabba.com and was not read in full. A CB Insights style aggregator lists a 120 thousand dollar seed in March 2017 with Y Combinator, Soma Capital and Multicoin Capital, and Caplight lists larger totals; both unverified single aggregator figures, so no round is recorded. The Wikipedia article says 2016 founding while YC says 2017. Founder background lines come from a search summary of the company About page that I did not open.
